inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: An estimated 8 million people turned out across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states for the "No Kings" protests against President Donald Trump's leadership, marking a clear escalation from the October actions with about a million more participants and 600 additional events. This powerful mobilization reflects a broad rejection of policies that deepen inequality, target vulnerable communities, and concentrate power while undermining labor rights and social protections. Far from any kind of coordinated disruption, it stands as a vital expression of resistance to systemic injustice and a demand for institutional reforms that prioritize equity and the needs of working people over entrenched privilege. These actions underscore the structural causes of ongoing harm and represent a necessary push to protect marginalized groups from policies rooted in historical inequality.
